jsesh.mdcDisplayer.draw
Class ElementDrawer

java.lang.Object
  jsesh.mdcDisplayer.draw.ElementDrawer
All Implemented Interfaces:
ModelElementVisitor
Direct Known Subclasses:
SimpleElementDrawer
public abstract class ElementDrawer
extends java.lang.Object
implements ModelElementVisitor

Object responsible for drawing the basic elements from a text. It doesn't need to deal at all with sub-elements. Note that it's called twice for each element, once with postfix= true, the other with posfix=false. Normally, you should draw in only one of these two cases. So the actual drawing methods might look like this one : 

 public void visitAlphabeticText(AlphabeticText t) {
		if (! postfix)
			return;
		if (t.getScriptCode() != ScriptCodes.COMMENT) {
			g.setFont(getDrawingSpecifications().getFont(t.getScriptCode()));
			g.drawString(t.getText().toString(), 0, g.getFontMetrics()
					.getAscent());
		}
	}

Method Detail

prepareDrawing

public void prepareDrawing(DrawingSpecifications drawingSpecifications)
Initialize the drawer before drawing the text. This method is called once before drawing a whole MDC text. implementations of ElementDrawer can override this method ; if so, they should call super.prepareDrawing(drawingSpecifications) at some time.

Parameters:
drawingSpecifications - TODO

cleanup

public void cleanup()
free some ressources used by ElementDrawer. called after the text has been drawn. Implementations can override this method, but should call super.cleanup() in this case.

drawElement

public void drawElement(MDCView e,
                        java.awt.Graphics2D g,
                        boolean postfix)
Draws the element part of a view on the Graphics element specified before. The graphic context is garanteed to be restored to its former value after a call to drawElement. So, in most cases, it's safe if the actual drawing methods modify g ; they don't need to restore it.

Parameters:
e - : the view to draw.
g - : the graphics to draw to.
postfix - : this boolean indicates if the method is being called after the subelements have been drawn.

isShadeAfter

setShadeAfter

public void setShadeAfter(boolean shadeAfter)
If ShadeAfter is true, the shading should be drawn after the shaded elements. For systems which support transparency, shadeAfter at true might be a good choice. Older systems (in the present case, wmf), should use shadeAfter= false.

shadeAfter -
